events.title: First Wave Carrier Strike Launch in Timor Sea
events.description: Vice Admiral Chuichi Nagumo's 1st Carrier Air Fleet (Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, Hiryu) launches 188 aircraft approximately 220 nautical miles north-northwest of Darwin. Strike commander Commander Mitsuo Fuchida leads the formation south-southeast.
events.evidenceBasis: Imperial Japanese Navy carrier operational logs and Senshi Sōsho Vol. 26.

events.title: USAAF P-40 Flight Turned Back by Weather
events.description: Ten P-40E Warhawks of the USAAF 33rd Pursuit Squadron led by Major Floyd Pell, which had departed Darwin for Koepang (Timor), encounter severe storm clouds over the Timor Sea and return to Darwin.
events.evidenceBasis: USAAF 33rd Pursuit Squadron records and Lowe Commission testimony.

events.title: Father McGrath Sighting and Radio Warning
events.description: Father John McGrath at Sacred Heart Mission, Bathurst Island, observes an immense formation of twin-engine and single-engine military aircraft overhead heading south-southeast. At 09:37 he transmits an urgent radio message to PMG coastal radio station VID Darwin: 'An unusually large air formation bearing south, heading south, observed over Bathurst Island.'
events.evidenceBasis: PMG transmission logs and Lowe Commission Exhibit 3.

events.title: Warning Handled at Operations and Sirens Withheld
events.description: The Bathurst Island message is received by PMG telegraphist and relayed to RAAF Operations at 09:40. Operations officers assess the report as referring to the ten returning American P-40s. Air raid sirens in Darwin are NOT ordered, leaving harbour shipping, wharf workers, and civilians entirely unwarned.
events.evidenceBasis: Lowe Commission findings and RAAF Operations logs.

events.title: Air Combat Over Darwin — USAAF P-40s Intercepted
events.description: As Major Pell's returning P-40s circle to land or patrol over Darwin, Japanese A6M2 Zeros dive out of the sun. Five P-40s are attacked in rapid succession; five others attempting to scramble from the runway are strafed and shot down. Major Pell and three other US pilots are killed.
events.evidenceBasis: USAAF action reports, RAAF diaries, and Lowe Commission.

events.title: First Bombs Fall on Darwin Harbour and Town
events.description: High-altitude Kate bombers release first salvos over Darwin Harbour and Stokes Hill. Dive-bombing Vals initiate steep runs against harbour shipping. The town air raid siren sounds at 10:01, three minutes after explosions begin.
events.evidenceBasis: Lowe Commission official findings (Justice Lowe fixed the initial bomb detonation at exactly 09:58).

events.title: Direct Bomb Hit on Darwin Post Office Shelter
events.description: A heavy bomb scores a direct hit on an open slit trench behind the Post Office building, instantly killing Postmaster H.A. Shugg's wife and daughter, telegraph supervisor, and six telephonists. All overseas civil telegraphic and telephonic communications with southern Australia are severed.
events.evidenceBasis: PMG records, CWGC civil dead roll, and Lowe Commission.

events.title: MV Neptuna Bombed at Stokes Hill Wharf
events.description: MV Neptuna, tied up to the wharf with 100 depth charges and 200 tons of explosives onboard, is struck by two bombs. Fires break out near the ammunition holds; crew and wharf labourers attempt to fight the blaze.

events.title: Coordinated Bombing of Harbour Shipping
events.description: Intense dive bombing and horizontal bombing across the anchorage. Hospital ship AHS Manunda is hit through the bridge and medical quarters (12 dead including Sister Margaret de Mestre). USS William B. Preston sustains bomb hit aft (14 dead). Zealandia, Meigs, Mauna Loa, and British Motorist are bombed and set on fire.
events.evidenceBasis: Naval logs, ship logs, and Lowe Commission.

events.title: USS Peary Targeted by Multiple Dive-Bomber Waves
events.description: USS Peary conducts radical evasive manoeuvres across the harbour at high speed. Targeted by multiple Val dive bombers, receiving five direct bomb hits. Fire rooms flooded, aft steering disabled, fantail ablaze. Crew fights guns until submerged.
events.evidenceBasis: US Navy official loss records and eyewitness accounts.

events.title: Catastrophic Detonation of MV Neptuna at Stokes Hill Wharf
events.description: Fire reaches depth charges and high-explosive ammunition in Neptuna's hold. The ship detonates in a massive explosion that obliterates the vessel, tears a 100-foot breach through the timber wharf deck, throws locomotive wagons into the sea, and kills 45 men instantly. Waterside workers on the severed section are trapped in burning oil.
events.evidenceBasis: Lowe Commission report and post-raid photographic surveys.

events.title: First Wave Carrier Strike Departs
events.description: Carrier aircraft reform and egress to the northwest over Beagle Gulf towards the carrier fleet in the Timor Sea. Harbour left burning with dense oil smoke; town in disarray. All-clear sounded at 11:10.
events.evidenceBasis: RAAF Operations log and Senshi Sōsho.

events.title: Second Raid — High-Altitude Bombing of RAAF Darwin
events.description: Fifty-four land-based twin-engine naval bombers (27 Bettys from Kendari and 27 Nells from Ambon) arrive at 18,000–23,000 feet. Flying in disciplined V-formations, they pattern-bomb RAAF Station Darwin, destroying runways, hangars, fuel dumps, and station buildings. Anti-aircraft batteries fire heavily but fail to break formation.
events.evidenceBasis: Senshi Sōsho, 14th Heavy AA Battery logs, and Lowe Commission.

events.title: USS Peary Sinks in Darwin Harbour
events.description: Having burned for over two hours following five bomb hits, destroyer USS Peary slips stern-first beneath the surface of Darwin Harbour in 27 meters of water. More than eighty American officers and sailors are lost (official sources record between 80 and 91 fatalities).
events.evidenceBasis: US Navy official action reports and surviving officer accounts.
